item.title: Embedding Voice in the Political Economy
item.content:encoded:
Sean O'Brady, McMaster University

Katherine Ravenswood, Auckland University of Technology

Tony Dundon, University of Limerick

Trine P. Larsen, University of Warwick

This special issue examines how employee voice functions within power structures and broader political economic systems. While voice has traditionally been studied as feedback and dialogue, the editors argue that insufficient attention has been paid to how voice relates to systemic inequalities, contemporary transformations like digitalisation and climate transitions, and shifting distributions of actor power. The call seeks critical, interdisciplinary research that theorizes voice as fundamentally embedded in political economic relations rather than treating external contexts as background factors.

Appel publié par British Journal of Industrial Relations. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.
